LESSON: KENYA’S BILL OF RIGHTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.3: Kenya’s Bill of Rights
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenya’s Bill of Rights, part of Political Developments and Governance in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we protect the special groups in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenya’s Bill of Rights together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: learners role-play situations/scenarios that bring out assertiveness in standing up for individual rights.

• Creativity and Imagination: learners design posters on human rights laws concerning special groups.

Values:
• Unity: learners display team spirit as they brainstorm on human rights laws for the protection of special groups.

• Patriotism: learners display a sense of responsibility to the nation as they develop strategies for promoting the protection of

special groups in the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Clubs and Societies: learners debate on human rights of special groups.

• Human Rights: learners brainstorm in groups on human rights laws for the protection of special groups.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners use Religious Education knowledge to develop strategies for promoting the protection of special groups in the

community.

• Learners apply English, Kiswahili, and Kenya Sign Language knowledge as they debate human laws for special groups.
